si.t: Section A — Household identification, eligibility and consent
Version: Draft 1 — for technical review and programming Reference period: 1 August 2024–31 July 2026 Phase 1: 1 August 2024–31 July 2025 Phase 2: 1 August 2025–31 July 2026
HOUSEHOLD — one form per selected household (Section A, C01, Section F)

To independently identify pregnancies and outcomes among eligible household members during the reference period and assess pregnancy notification and follow-up. Findings will subsequently be reconciled with KASSEP records.
Interview only households selected through the approved sampling procedure. Do not replace absent or refusing households without supervisor authorisation under the sampling protocol.
├── ⟳ WOMAN × hh_eligible_women (A21) — Section B roster → D1 consent → D2 screening
Complete household identification, consent and the female roster before individual pregnancy interviews.
Include eligible women regardless of marital status, relationship to the household head or known pregnancy history.
│ └── ⟳ PREGNANCY × pregnancy_number (D10) — E1 timing/outcome, E3 maternal survival, E4 notification
Include women who died or moved away after living in the household during the reference period.
⟳ HOUSEHOLD (Level 1) — one form per selected household → data sheet: HH_Data
Interview women directly and privately wherever possible. Arrange a revisit before using a proxy for an unavailable woman, where feasible.
│ └── ⟳ BABY × babies_number (E11) — E2 baby record (only when E10 = 1 birth)
Do not ask a household respondent to disclose another woman’s pregnancy history in a group setting.
Do not read response categories unless instructed.
└── ⟳ DEATH × each death reported (C01 = 1) — C02–C10 death roster
Record “do not know” rather than guessing. Never invent dates.
Pause or stop if a respondent becomes distressed or requests it.
Apply approved consent and assent procedures for participants below the age of independent consent.
A household is a group of people that share a living space and eat from the same pot.
General codes: 1 Yes | 0 No | 8 Do not know | 9 Declined Use these only where specified. Numeric counts and dates must have separate missing-response options.

Hello. My name is [NAME], and I am working with Doctors Medical Aid Foundation (DMAF). We are assessing how pregnancies, births, and deaths were recorded in this community between August 2024 and July 2026.

I would first like to ask who lived in this household during that time. We may then invite eligible women to answer a short questionnaire privately. We may also ask about household members who died. With permission, selected details will be compared with surveillance records.

Participation is voluntary. You may decline any question or stop the interview. Your decision will not affect any services or benefits. Information will be kept confidential and reported without identifying you.

If you have questions, you may contact Amina Sabu on 08144435403. May I continue?

A21 hh_eligible_women is the repeat count for the Section B roster (it serves the same purpose as the form's C1_roster_count). C2_roster_count_validation confirms no eligible woman was missed before closing the loop.
Each child record carries its parent key(s), so every level can be joined back: Baby → Pregnancy → Woman → Household.
A death record may refer to a rostered woman or a pregnancy (C02 instruction / E3 referral) — link it by woman_line instead of creating a duplicate.
The data sheets have check columns that count child rows against the loop count and flag "Mismatch".

Ask every consenting household, including those with no women on the roster.
Between 1 August 2024 and 31 July 2026, did anyone who belonged to this household die, including a baby who lived only briefly?
Any household death during the reference period?
Yes → death roster; otherwise Section D

⟳ REPEAT: DEATH (Level 2) — repeats for each reported death when C01=1 → data sheet: Deaths_Data
Link to woman/pregnancy record where applicable

Was she pregnant when she died?
Ask for female deaths potentially within reproductive ages
Did a pregnancy end during the six weeks before she died, whether through childbirth, miscarriage or another pregnancy loss?
Yes if C08=1, C09=1, or pregnancy relationship remains uncertain
Do not use proxy to bypass refusal
Ask a short clarifying question where age is uncertain; do not dismiss a possible pregnancy-associated death because an age field is missing.
Babies born without signs of life are captured through pregnancy outcomes, not counted again as deaths after live birth.

This screen identifies cases for verification; it does not establish clinical maternal cause of death.

We are assessing whether pregnancies and their outcomes were recorded correctly between August 2024 and July 2026. I would like to ask about pregnancies during that period and whether anyone contacted you to monitor them. Some questions concern pregnancy losses or deaths. You may skip any question or stop at any time. With your permission, selected details will later be compared with surveillance records. Your answers will be kept confidential. May I continue?
For proxies, adapt pronouns and explain that only information they know should be provided. Apply separate approved assent/permission procedures where needed.
⟳ INSIDE WOMAN REPEAT (Level 2) — D10 pregnancy_number sets the Pregnancy repeat count → data sheet: Women_Data
Between 1 August 2024 and 31 July 2026, were you pregnant at any time? Include a pregnancy that began before August 2024 but continued into the period.
During that period, was there any pregnancy that ended before delivery, including a miscarriage or another pregnancy loss?
During that period, did you give birth, including to a baby born without signs of life or a baby who died soon after birth?
Altogether, how many different pregnancies overlapped that period? Count twins or other multiple births as one pregnancy.
Any yes → create episodes; all no → close individual interview
For proxy interviews: Replace “you” with “[NAME]”. Record uncertainty; do not interpret a proxy’s lack of knowledge as “no pregnancy.”
⟳ REPEAT: PREGNANCY (Level 3, inside Woman) — loops pregnancy_number (D10) times; E11 sets the Baby repeat count → data sheet: Pregnancy_Data
Repeat for each pregnancy overlapping the reference period.
I will ask a few questions about each pregnancy, beginning with the most recent.
⟳ REPEAT: BABY (Level 4, inside Pregnancy) — loops babies_number (E11) times when E10=1 → data sheet: Baby_Data
⟳ INSIDE PREGNANCY REPEAT (Level 3) — once per pregnancy episode → data sheet: Pregnancy_Data
Repeat for every baby from the pregnancy.
For direct interviews with a living woman, record current survival automatically. Do not ask her whether she died.
Around what month and year did this pregnancy begin?
By 31 July 2026, had this pregnancy ended, or was it still ongoing?
Has this pregnancy ended since then?
Ask for all ended pregnancies, not only live births
About how many weeks or months pregnant were you when it ended?
Where were you usually living during this pregnancy?
Where were you usually living when the pregnancy ended?
How many babies were born from this pregnancy?
Note: Do not ask the respondent to apply a technical stillbirth definition. Record signs of life and pregnancy duration for subsequent classification.
Did she die while pregnant, during childbirth, or after the pregnancy ended?
How long after the pregnancy ended did she die?
Referral: Death during pregnancy/childbirth, within 42 days after any pregnancy ending, or uncertain timing → mortality-verification tool. Link to Section C to avoid duplicate cases.
After birth, did the baby show any sign of life—for example, breathing, crying or movement?
Was a heartbeat or pulsation of the cord noticed, even if the baby did not cry or breathe?
Ask where any sign of life reported
How long did the baby live?
Number + days/months; less than one day; unknown
Is a birth, delivery or other relevant record available and may we view it?
Do not require documents for inclusion
Routing: All babies completed → E3. Suspected stillbirth or uncertain signs of life → verification flag.
Ask for each episode, adapting pronouns for proxies.
Did anyone in the community contact you about this pregnancy to record it or monitor how it was progressing?
Multiple: community leader/WDC; Scribe; FSO; facility worker; other; role unknown
⟳ HOUSEHOLD (Level 1) — once per household; F01=0 returns to the Pregnancy repeat → data sheet: HH_Data
When did they first contact you?
What did they ask or do?
Multiple: recorded pregnancy/details; asked about progress; recorded outcome; checked maternal survival; checked baby survival; provided clinical care only; other; unknown
Distinguish surveillance from routine clinical care
After the pregnancy ended, did anyone contact you or the household to ask what happened to you and, where relevant, the baby?
Ask all ended episodes, including losses
Was there any such contact six weeks or more after the pregnancy ended?
What did they check during follow-up?
Multiple: pregnancy outcome; woman’s health/survival; baby’s health/survival; other; unknown
Did you or someone in the household tell a community reporting person about the pregnancy or outcome?
Was there any difficulty reporting the pregnancy or outcome or receiving follow-up?
Multiple where needed; brief explanation only
Interviewer note: Contact recalled by a household is not proof that a KASSEP record exists or that formal follow-up was completed. These are assessed through reconciliation.
“Have we included every pregnancy during the period, including any loss or baby who lived only briefly?”
Short text; no unnecessary sensitive narrative

If F01 identifies another pregnancy, return to Section E. Thank respondents and explain any agreed follow-up. Obtain separate consent for mortality verification rather than assuming this interview covers it.
